status: Closed model/canonical codec; native admission, physical Archive layout and Index consumers require integration qualification.
envelope: Existing Fact: SourceRecordId, record_kind, record_schema_version, visibility QualifiedRef, recorded_at, payload. SHA-256 uses the existing bigbrotr/fact/1\0 domain.
encoding: Deterministic CBOR profile 1. Exact definite arrays, shortest integers, native booleans, required explicit nulls. No maps, floats, arbitrary JSON, exception text or extension slots.
model_memory: Measurement owns one fixed boxed record allocated through checked reservation. Decoder charges its required logical bytes before allocation. Callers separately fund inline values, input/output and every clone; allocator overhead/process RSS require runtime qualification. Canonical bytes do not include this ownership detail.
counter_invariants: rx_ws_bytes counts actually consumed WS framing plus payload octets, excluding HTTP/TLS overhead. rx_payload_bytes counts the consumed payload subset, excluding frame headers, and must not exceed rx_ws_bytes. Declared potential lengths are neither counter.

Known first valid EVENT, EOSE delivery, AUTH and correlated CLOSED are distinct NIP-01 envelope kinds. Count each known observation once: rx_messages, rx_physical_frames and rx_payload_bytes must each be at least that sum. This is a conservative minimum, not a reconstruction of total traffic or exact message sizes.
A known first valid event requires event_candidates >= 1. A known completed REQ flush requires tx_ws_bytes > 0. A non-null phase/moment with null clock samples is still a known observation.

The same invariants apply to CompletionUnknown and terminal/resolution observations. TCP/upgrade-only prefixes with no WS message or request observations may retain all-zero counters. Incomplete or unclassified input may have received bytes/frames but no complete message observation. No relation to configured cap values is imposed and observed cap crossings remain representable.
profile_interpretation: One exact REQ filter {kinds:[1],limit:1}; generated subscription identity is correlation, not another profile.

Open timeout begins at authorized connector entry and ends at validated upgrade. Open observation elapsed times instead anchor after the first externally directed connect syscall returned, including a DNS resolver connect.

Nominal timeout is not authorization. Effective authority ceiling is fixed with intent, not changing remaining time or a renewal promise. Its expiry is authority interruption, not remote timeout. Cleanup may make terminal elapsed time exceed the I/O authority ceiling.
No compression, signed AUTH response, publication, implicit retry or address fallback. DNS transport is TCP; inherited limits do not implement DNS catalog measurements.
The event cap is normalized signed-event JSON size. Raw JSON with ignored extensions remains subject to the larger message/parser limits.

All physical WS header/payload traffic, including controls, unrelated/rejected input and teardown, contributes to aggregate limits. Actual observed counters are not declared potential lengths and are not clipped to caps. No arithmetic equality between independent counters/caps is imposed by this representation.
proof_and_resolution: Constructors validate structure only. A trusted adapter observes the actual externally directed connect syscall return (accepted or immediate error) and samples afterward; intent, timestamp, socket allocation, future construction and generic first poll are not that proof. No packet/remote-receipt inference follows.

ExecutionUnknown has no fabricated actual timing. CompletionUnknown has an actual-start claim and fixed partial observations, but no terminal reason. Runtime production of CompletionUnknown requires durably recoverable trusted start evidence; a lost RAM capture still recovers ExecutionUnknown.

UTC samples can be null or regress; elapsed samples use a separate monotonic clock and cannot invert known phase order. Zero UTC and zero elapsed are valid and distinct from null. Known completion with unavailable timing is a non-null moment containing null fields.

REQ anchor is completed local flush. EVENT and EOSE anchors are decoder completion before parsing/verification, not kernel arrival. EOSE delivery may precede prefix verification. Positive EOSE requires eose_prefix_verified. First valid event retains both original delivery and verification completion. Empty EOSE has no first-event value.

Resolution requires the exact prior unknown FactRef, same dataset, visibility, attempt ID, subject/observer/route/access/method, immutable profile and clock ID. Quality details may change. Same-stream target sequence must be earlier; cross-stream recovery requires consumer-verified causality.

Resolution preserves previously known start/call result, phase moments, first event identity, true flags and nondecreasing counters; null samples can be filled. It cannot target a terminal or another resolution. The helper validates the supplied target, not target availability, durable authority, causal completeness or conflict freedom.

Consumers apply the selected cut before resolution, retain unresolved uncertainty, count the same attempt once and expose competing terminal conflicts. They must not select by latest recorded_at/arrival. Resolution FactRefs are strong dependencies, separate from dictionary refs and event corrects.

All six payload dictionary references and envelope visibility are required. Resolve exact endpoint/observer/direct-route/access/passive-method/clock descriptors; parsing a namespace does not establish a mapping, allocation, scope or dispatch permission.
future_subjects: RecipientMetadataHttp remains selected P04-T14 work; future subjects and catalog child types require versioned closed producer/consumer contracts.
qualification: Independent literal vectors cover this layout. Rust execution, admission/replay, physical Archive/Index integration, trusted runtime capture, crash behavior and full Monitor scheduling are separate gates; this contract does not mark those tasks complete.
